Focused directory rename heuristic slice maps renamed internal plugin entry files during directory rename similarity scoring. Focused SSH receive-pack adapter slice maps ssh:// and scp-like URL parsing, git-receive-pack command quoting, and injected stream handoff without shelling out to ssh. Focused smart HTTP auth/session slice maps caller-supplied auth headers, managed header validation, Git-Protocol propagation on POST, and Set-Cookie propagation from discovery to receive-pack POST. Focused smart HTTP redirect slice maps gix-transport redirect base-url reconciliation, same-authority redirects, safe http-to-https upgrades, effective-base reuse for POST, and rejection of cross-host or downgrade redirects. Focused smart HTTP proxy slice maps http.proxy-style proxy selection, noProxy matching, Basic proxy credentials from URLs or explicit options, credential-helper callback boundaries, and PHP stream-context proxy wiring without leaking proxy authorization into origin headers. Focused strict-best rename heuristic slice maps Gitoxide rewrite tracking behavior where a renamed directory is selected from similar candidates only when one target is strictly best, preserving ambiguity rejection for equal candidates. Focused directory rename target-collision slice maps a renamed WordPress plugin directory colliding with an independently added target directory while the old directory is modified. wordpressScenario: Git-backed WordPress content workflows, package installs, Playground snapshots, and server-side repo primitives; current examples parse a WordPress deploy tree, write/read HEAD plus deployment branch refs, inspect packed branch/tag refs, parse protocol v2 ls-refs discovery responses, build a shallow blobless ref-in-want fetch request, parse protocol v2 fetch response sections and sideband pack/progress/error bytes, orchestrate a protocol v1 send-pack flow from advertised refs through generated branch/tag pack request and status response, build thin REF_DELTA send-pack payloads against remote WordPress base objects, run receive-pack handshake/request/response cycles over native stream, git-daemon, smart HTTP auth/session/redirect/proxy, and SSH command adapters, resolve loose+packed refs, locate compacted object offsets through pack indexes and multi-pack-indexes, use MIDX-backed object database pack selection/de-duplication, read delta-resolved packed commit/blob objects, track blobless partial-clone promisor state for omitted media objects, lazily hydrate promised media objects into loose storage, apply sparse checkout materialization to a plugin-focused WordPress tree, recursively merge nested WordPress metadata/theme blobs with Git index v2 conflict-stage writes, checkout-clean merged worktree marker-file output, stale file removal, .git metadata preservation, directory-file tree-stage index expansion, exact same-object rename/delete and rename/rename conflicts, bounded similar-blob rename/delete and rename/modify conflicts for renamed plugin entry files, same-target rename content merges at the renamed plugin path, bounded directory rename/modify merges for renamed plugin directories, directory rename heuristics that match renamed plugin entry files and choose strict-best forked plugin directory candidates, and pack+loose+alternate object database traversal with replacement refs without shelling out to git. The latest merge case detects a WordPress plugin directory rename whose new slug collides with an independently added plugin directory while the old slug is modified, preserving conflict stages instead of dropping either side. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-add case, where one side modifies the old path and adds the rename target while the other side renames the old path to that target. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-add-symlink case, preserving stages when a same-target rename collides with a symlink added by the other side. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-add-same-symlink case, where a symlink rename and an independently added identical symlink at the new path resolve cleanly. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-rename-plus-content case, where both sides rename one file to different targets while changing content, preserving ancestor-path conflict stages. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-add-exe-bit-conflict case, where a mode-only edit on the old executable path combines with the other side replacing it through a rename, resolving cleanly to the non-executable file. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-add-delete case, where one side deletes the old path and adds the rename target while the other side renames the old path to that target, leaving target-path conflict markers and stage 2/3 entries. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-rename-delete-delete case, where each side renames a different old path to the same new path while deleting the other, preserving one target-path conflict with stage 2/3 entries. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline remove-executable-mode case, where one side removes the executable bit while the other edits file content, resolving cleanly to edited non-executable content. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers the gix-merge tree-baseline rename-delete case, where a file renamed into an old directory is replayed under the other side's directory rename and then conflicts on content at the relocated path. The latest upstream fixture mappings cover symlink-modification, symlink-addition, and type-change-to-symlink conflict staging while keeping the ours symlink in the merged tree, matching local Git oracle behavior. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers rename-and-modification clean resolution by carrying content edits from a nested old path onto the renamed file path. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers no-merge-base add/add conflict output for unrelated histories, keeping stage 2/3 entries and materializing marker content for the shared path. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers change-and-delete modify/delete output, preserving the modified regular file and symlink-replacement file in the merged tree with ancestor/ours index stages. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers type-change-and-renamed rename/type-change output, preserving both the old-path replacement file and the renamed symlink with target-path unmerged stages. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers added-file-changed-content-and-mode add/add output, including executable merged worktree conflict content and original side stages. The latest upstream fixture mapping covers renamed-symlink-with-conflict output, keeping both renamed symlinks while the shared edited file resolves cleanly.
